leads.posting: Edtech startup Arivihan raises $10 Mn in Series A led by Accel and Prosus. Bengaluru- based edtech startup Arivihan has raised $10 million in Series A funding from existing investors Accel and Prosus Ventures, along with an additional $200,000 from its existing GSF angel investors. The round takes the company’s total funding to more than $15 million. Entrackr recently reported on the company’s new funding and estimated that its valuation had jumped 3.3X to around $60 million. The fresh capital will be used to expand into new states and strengthen its presence in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Bihar. The company also plans to expand its CBSE offering, develop more vernacular language capabilities and increase its AI research efforts. Founded in 2022 by Ritesh Singh Chandel, Sonu Kumar and Rushabh Kothari, Arivihan offers an AI based learning platform for school students. Its platform provides interactive video lessons, instant doubt solving and AI driven study plans without relying on live teachers. The company currently serves students preparing for State Board, CBSE and NEET exams, with a focus on students from tier 2, tier 3 cities and rural areas. Arivihan said around 80% of its subscribers come from tier 3 cities and rural India. Arivihan will also scale its digital marketing and on ground distribution network as it expands across India. The company plans to hire across key functions and launch new crash courses. Arivihan was previously part of Accel’s Atoms accelerator programme and received seed funding through the programme in March 2024. The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Arivihan’s revenue jumped nearly 14.8X to Rs 3.14 crore from Rs 21.29 lakh in FY24, while the company posted a loss of Rs 4.45 crore.

Tom is a skilled thoroughbred handicapper and heard he could get better horse statistics online. Instead of talking about horse racing, Constantino shared his vision with Tom for bringing manufacturing onto the Internet. Tom asked, "what do people even do on the Internet?" and Constantino responded by showing him a few web sites. The septuagenarian said "that's interesting," closed his first laptop, went home, and surprised Constantino when he visited his office the following morning with a notepad of plans for the two of them to start an Internet manufacturing company together. "What do people even do on the Internet?" Tom Cummings, co-founder, 2009 3 months later, Sticker Mule was born. Neither Tom nor Anthony had plans to sell stickers, all they wanted to do was build a modern manufacturing company that had a close connection with customers to align the success of the business with the performance of the factory floor. Of course, the two had never done anything on the Internet before so they did what anyone would do when trying to learn how to do something new. They looked up experts, found one that had a phone number and made a phone call. "We want your help to build an Internet company," the two informed Software CEO, Sean Schofield, who accepted the call and was well respected for being the creator of a prestigious open-source ecommerce platform called Spree . Schofield asked what they wanted to sell, but they hadn't decided on a product yet nor did they have a budget in mind. The confused Spree CEO tried to end the call but Anthony interjected, "well we have $100,000 to build a site" which provoked an invitation to get started. Constantino designed his concept for an online ordering process for a manufacturing company but still hadn't decided on a product when he first met his new software development team that accepted the $100,000 project. "We can get started immediately if you pick a product," Schofield insisted at their meeting. Constantino went home, talked to his brother Nicholas who also joined to help the project, and the two settled on stickers after combining various iterations of animal plus product. leads.title: Software + FDE + AI Engineers
leads.posting: Balerion AI | Software + FDE + AI Engineers | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE | Full-time | $250k+ base + seed equity | Visa sponsorship available | https://balerion.ai We're building agentic AI for mortgage lending — automating document processing and income qualification for loan originators. Underwriting a loan means pulling numbers out of a few hundred pages of paystubs, W-2s, bank statements, and tax returns, then applying underwriting guidelines that run to thousands of pages of edge cases. Most of it is still done by hand. Problems we actually work on: routing scanned pages to OCR vs. text extraction when the text layer is unreliable; extraction pipelines where a wrong number is much worse than a missing one; running long agent workflows durably so a failure three steps in doesn't restart the whole loan; and evaluating multi-step output against guidelines that are themselves ambiguous. We put real effort into eval infrastructure, because "the demo looked good" does not survive contact with a lender's compliance team. Stack: Python, PydanticAI, Restate for durable execution, Postgres, AWS. Frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic plus open-source models where they win on cost or latency. We raised an $8M seed led by Kleiner Perkins and have paying customers in production. Team previously at Snowflake, PayPal, Twitter, Atlassian, and Microsoft. Comp: $250k+ base, meaningful seed-stage equity, 5% 401(k) match, full health coverage, commuter stipend, gym membership, daily office breakfast & lunch. Full relocation to SF covered. Onsite in SF. Visa sponsorship: yes. Email hiring@balerion.ai with "HN" in the subject, plus a resume or GitHub.
